Brent future $93.19 (▲0.5%) Thu 12 Nov 07:18 UK · BRNT $96.51 · CRUD $16.91 — Wed 11 Nov close

Open the map page

1
East-West pipeline hit, Medina region (9 Nov)
Saudi Energy Ministry: an attack caused a limited fire on the pipeline in the Medina region, put out with operations unaffected; exact spot not given (approximate).
2
Missiles intercepted over Riyadh (10 Nov)
The coalition says a ballistic and a cruise missile were downed over Riyadh on 10 Nov, after debris damaged the Aramco Tower on 8 Nov; no output loss reported.
3
10 Hormuz crossings (10 Nov), 5 dark
Windward counted 10 crossings on 10 Nov (one tanker) against 84-140 a day pre-war; Kpler put October Hormuz crude at about 10.2 mb/d, 60% of pre-war (area approximate).
4
UAE exports ~4.4 mb/d (9 Nov), up from 3.2
A UAE official says exports are almost 4.4 mb/d vs 3.1-3.2 mb/d before the war, helped by the Habshan-Fujairah pipeline that avoids Hormuz.
5
Tankers hit 10-11 Nov, incl. 19 nm NE of Lima
UKMTO: a tanker struck about 19 nm north-east of Lima, Oman on 10 Nov; the VLCC Fujairah Energy was hit in the Gulf the same day (4 crew injured) and the Saudi-flagged NCC FAJR was hit in the strait on 11 Nov (exact spots not given).
6
36 ships holding in Gulf (11 Nov), down from 57
straits.live counted 36 AIS-visible ships holding in the Strait and Gulf watch box at 20:30 UTC on 11 Nov, against 57 on 10 Nov and 197 on 4 Nov; it says the fall reflects weaker AIS reception, not ships leaving (area approximate).
7
Bypass routes >40% of Gulf exports
Kpler: pipelines avoiding Hormuz carry over 40% of regional exports vs 17% pre-war; Yanbu loadings 2.21 mb/d in 1-25 Oct vs 2.54 in September.
GULF OIL FLOWS · updated 12 Nov 2026

Less oil is leaving the Gulf than before the war: Kpler counts about 16.1 mb/d of crude across Hormuz, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Oman in October, of which only about 10.2 mb/d went through Hormuz itself, about 60% of the 17.1 mb/d pre-war level. Traffic through the strait stays very thin (Windward: 10 crossings on 10 Nov, half of them dark), so bypass routes carry over 40% of exports and the UAE says its exports have risen to almost 4.4 mb/d via Fujairah. Attacks continued: a Liberia-flagged VLCC was hit in the Gulf on 10 Nov with four crew hurt and the Saudi-flagged tanker NCC FAJR was hit in a possible attack in the strait on 11 Nov. Risk rose again mid-week: Iran rejected a US plan to move its enriched uranium abroad, its negotiator Ghalibaf said Hormuz will 'never return' to pre-war status, and Israel's security cabinet reportedly ordered the army to prepare a possible attack on Iran; Brent edged back up to about $93.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf; Mohsen Rezaei — Iran Parliament Speaker and lead negotiator; Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council
“What stands in the way of an agreement is our lack of trust in the United States.”
Why it matters: Rejecting a core US nuclear demand stalls the deal that markets had priced after Trump called the war 'effectively over', keeping Hormuz closed longer; Trump says he is ready to resume war if the Qatari track fails.
